intro: Deep in the Istranca forest, stone arches rise among the trees. You are at the Kurşunlugerme Aqueduct, in Kırklareli province, from the 4th–5th century AD. This is the longest surviving stretch of the line that carried water to Constantinople, and its design is rare: it carries two separate channels, one above the other.
history: Here in the Istranca forest stands the longest surviving stretch of the line that once carried water to Constantinople, and that main line alone ran for some 250 kilometres. What makes this aqueduct special? It carries two separate channels stacked one above the other, so that water from different springs reached the city without mixing.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the two stacked channels and the arcade that carries them. Look at the channel section, and then follow the forest route.
facts: Did you know? The water line to Constantinople is the longest known aqueduct system of the Roman world. With the branches added to the main line later, the whole system runs to more than 400 kilometres. And here the aqueduct carries two channels one above the other, so water from different springs reached the city without ever mixing.
outro: This brings our tour of the Kurşunlugerme Aqueduct to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this quiet forest keep its old stones for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
